title: The Neat desk by the window
subtitle: 习惯自律 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）
meta: 主题语境：习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）　|　核心词汇：neat　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 neat 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the researcher wrote of ① a neat desk by the window in the paper, and everybody in the lab said at once that it was ② neater than the one named there the year before. Three terms on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the researcher, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the neat ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the neatest desk by the window anybody in the lab had ever seen, or so the paper for February 1954 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too neat to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the student who had come to help; the neat ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the tube at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a neat trick with the cards, and said that no student in his right mind would call it ⑥ as neat as the trick with the cards they had once had in the old lab. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was neat or not, and he said so.

By 1967 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the paper. What the line asked for was ⑦ something neat, and nothing besides. The student from the next lab called the whole plan ⑧ quite neat; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the paper kept the names of the neat ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1970, for the whole place, she wrote of another neat desk by the window in the same paper, and the work, which took two terms, seemed ⑨ neater than anybody had expected. ⑩ The neatest trick with the cards in the whole lab, she said in 1972, was the one she could never quite name; the neat ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 整洁（前置定语 a neat desk by the window：1960 年研究员在研究报告里记下的那件整洁的书桌）
B. adj. 整洁／利落（比较级 neater than：文中两处，一处比窗边整洁的书桌，一处比预想）
C. adj. 整洁／利落（最高级 the neatest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 整洁（表语 too neat to do：母亲觉得它太整洁，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 利落（前置定语 a neat trick with the cards：叔叔把整件事称作一桩利落的手法）
F. adj. 利落（同级比较 as neat as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩牌桌上利落的手法相比）
G. adj. 利落（后置定语 something neat：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 利落（受程度副词修饰 quite neat：那位学生的评价）

items.q: a neat desk by the window
the neatest desk by the window anybody
a neat trick with the cards
The neatest trick with the cards in

answers.why: neat 意为“整洁”，1960 年研究员在研究报告里记下的是“一件整洁的书桌”，此处作前置定语 a neat desk by the window。
neat 意为“整洁”，此处用比较级 neater than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
neat 意为“整洁”，研究报告上 二月 那行字说它是实验室里最整洁的一件，故用最高级 the neatest desk by the window。
neat 意为“整洁”，母亲认为这件东西“太整洁了，谁也用不上”，too neat to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
neat 意为“利落”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩利落的手法”，此处作前置定语 a neat trick with the cards。
neat 意为“利落”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩牌桌上利落的手法一样利落”，同级比较用 as neat as。
neat 意为“利落”，研究报告上那半行字要的是“利落的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something neat。
neat 意为“利落”，邻实验室来的那位学生认为这套计划“相当利落”，quite 修饰原级 neat。
neat 意为“利落”，1970 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要利落”，故用比较级 neater than。
neat 意为“利落”，母亲 1972 年说的是“整个实验室里最利落的那一桩”，故用最高级 the neatest trick with the cards。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1960 年，研究员在研究报告里记下了一件整洁的书桌。（a neat desk by the window）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更整洁。（neater than …）
母亲觉得它太整洁，谁也用不上。（too neat to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩利落的手法。（a neat trick with the cards）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩牌桌上利落的手法一样利落。（as neat as …）
到了 1967 年，研究报告上只剩半行字：要的是一件利落的东西。（something neat）
answers: In 1960 the researcher wrote of a neat desk by the window in the paper.
Everybody said it was neater than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too neat to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a neat trick with the cards.
He said nobody would call it as neat as the trick with the cards they had once had.
By 1967 the paper asked for nothing but something neat.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 neat 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1960 the researcher wrote of a neat desk by the window in the paper, and nobody forgot it.
It was the neatest desk by the window in the lab, or so the paper says.
My mother thought it too neat to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a neat trick with the cards, and nobody argued with him.
The student from the next lab called the plan quite neat, and everybody laughed.
The neat ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
